title: Bug Blindness
summary: Dan Luu's essay explores the phenomenon of 'bug blindness' - how developers become blind to obvious bugs in their own code due to cognitive biases, familiarity with the codebase, and assumption-driven thinking. The article draws from real-world examples and psychological research to explain why even experienced engineers miss simple issues that would be obvious to others.
problem_solved: Explains why developers often overlook obvious bugs in their own code and how to recognize this cognitive trap.
why_valuable: Understanding bug blindness helps developers develop better debugging strategies and awareness of cognitive limitations in code review processes.
